idee_recherchee.texte: Time passes more slowly for an astronaut orbiting Earth or for a clock near a massive object than for someone far from gravity, an effect called time dilation that has been measured with atomic clocks and must be corrected in GPS satellites.

titre_video: Scientists Are Freaking Out Over Space Time (It's Not Real)
titre: Des trous noirs qui grossissent et dilatation du temps à l'horizon
resume: Black holes almost never lose mass and keep growing as matter falls in. An outside observer sees an infalling object slow, redden and appear to freeze at the horizon, even though it crosses in normal time unaware of this.
texte: What makes black holes [music] so terrifying is that they almost never lose weight. Every piece of matter that falls in just makes [music] them bigger and more dangerous. And worst of all, they are incredibly patient. When you get close to a black hole, time doesn't just slow down, it gets tortured. If you watched an object approaching a black hole's event horizon, you would see it slow down, becoming redder, dimmer, [music] and more distorted. From your perspective, it would appear to freeze at the edge, its final moments stretched across eternity. You would literally watch it fade away over billions of years, never [music] quite crossing the line. But in reality, the object fell through the event horizon in normal time, completely unaware that outside the universe sees them as frozen. >> [music] >>
